options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Claisen Condensation specifically denotes: The base-promoted reaction between two ester molecules to yield a β-keto ester through nucleophilic acyl substitution.

options.label: B
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Claisen Condensation is properly defined as: The rapid constitutional isomerization between a carbonyl compound (keto form) and an unsaturated alcohol (enol form) catalyzed by acid or base.

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Claisen Condensation is properly defined as: The carbon atom positioned directly adjacent to a carbonyl group, whose attached α-hydrogens possess enhanced acidity (pKa ~ 16–20).

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Claisen Condensation is properly defined as: The resonance-stabilized ambident anion generated by deprotonating the α-carbon of a carbonyl compound, possessing nucleophilic reactivity at carbon and oxygen.
